newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers for Central Park killers ask for more time.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers for Central Park killers ask for more time.

text.p: Lawyers for two teenagers accused in a Central Park slaying asked the court Wednesday for more time to conduct a preliminary investigation before prosecutors present the case to a grand jury for action.
"This is a complicated case. We need time to sort things out," said Benjamin Brafman, a prominent criminal defence lawyer hired by the wealthy parents of Daphne Abdela.

Abdela and her boyfriend Christopher Vasquez, both 15, were charged with second degree murder and robbery of Michael McMorrow, 44, a real estate agent. His body was found floating face up in a lake in Central Park Friday morning.
The medical examiner said McMorrow was stabbed about 30 times including in the neck, face, chest, jugular vein, heart and lungs. His hands were severed at the wrist.

Abdela's lawyer said the reason he waived the five-day time limit in which prosecutors must report whether they plan to indict a suspect is "because in my judgment, the district attorney may be acting on inaccurate information. I don't want an indictment for a murder in a case where I think the defendant did not commit murder."
Arnold Kriss, the lawyer representing Vasquez, would not answer questions after his client's arraignment.
Vasquez, who was under a suicide watch while undergoing psychiatric evaluation at Bellevue Hospital since his arrest last week, made his first court appearance Wednesday.
The slightly built, bespectacled youth, his right little finger heavily bandaged in a huge splint, appeared dazed as officers led him into the courtroom.
His lawyer requested Vasquez be continued under a suicide watch when he is transfered to Spofford Juvenile Detention Centre. Abdela was also being detained at the juvenile centre.
Abdela was the adopted daughter of Angelo and Catherine Abdela. He is a businessman and she is a former French model and they live in a $2 million apartment on Central Park West.
On the night of the murder, police said the teenagers spent the evening drinking beer and malt liquor with McMorrow.
During a hearing Saturday for Abdela, prosecutors said she admitted watching Vasquez stab McMorrow. She also said she ordered Vasquez to "gut his body. He will sink. He's a fatty."
The two teenagers were due back in court June 16.
